title: Application of Neuroscience Tools in Building Construction – An Interdisciplinary Analysis

findings.antecedent: cold indoor temperatures
findings.consequent: negative effect on cardiovascular health
findings.quote: research has revealed that cold indoor temperatures have a negative effect on cardiovascular health (Umishio et al., 2021)

findings.antecedent: ambient temperature and human thermal sensation
findings.consequent: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
findings.quote: HRV is sensitive to changes in ambient temperature and human thermal sensation and may be utilized as a potential physiological indicator of human thermal comfort (Liu et al., 2008).

findings.antecedent: significant thermal sensation or thermal discomfort
findings.consequent: sympathetic nerves in a more active state, triggering stress and anxiety
findings.quote: When thermal sensation is significant or thermal discomfort is present, sympathetic nerves are in a more active state and can trigger emotions such as stress and anxiety (Yang et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: higher levels of indoor exposure to carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and ozone
findings.consequent: elevated HRV, decreased parasympathetic regulation, increased sympathetic drive
findings.quote: studies have demonstrated that higher levels of indoor exposure to carbon monoxide (Riojas-Rodriguez et al., 2006), carbon dioxide (Zhang et al., 2021), and ozone (Huang et al., 2019) result in elevated HRV, as reflected by decreased parasympathetic regulation (RMSSD, HF, pNN50) and increased sympathetic drive (SDNN, LF, LF/HF)

findings.antecedent: increased exposure to indoor particle pollutants, especially PM2.5
findings.consequent: decreased HRV levels, increased cardiovascular risk
findings.quote: increased exposure to indoor particle pollutants, especially PM2.5, causes HRV levels to decrease (Cavallari et al., 2007), thus increasing cardiovascular risk (Jia et al., 2012).

findings.antecedent: LF/HF ratio of viewing plants of different colors
findings.consequent: human satisfaction
findings.quote: it is demonstrated that the LF/HF ratio of viewing plants of different colors is significantly negatively correlated to human satisfaction, demonstrating that HRV is a valid physiological parameter for assessing the comfort provided by indoor plants (Qin et al., 2014).

findings.antecedent: indoor plants
findings.consequent: human comfort, mental stress, happiness, physiological and psychological effects
findings.quote: scholars explored the effects of indoor plants on human comfort, mental stress, happiness as well as other physiological and psychological effects (Hassan et al., 2020; Elsadek and Liu, 2021)

findings.antecedent: different plants and colors in outdoor green spaces and the layout of green landscape
findings.consequent: mental health
findings.quote: effects of different plants and colors in outdoor green spaces and the layout of green landscape on mental health (Huang et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: physical and mental fatigue among construction workers
findings.consequent: safety hazards (trips, falls, impacts)
findings.quote: EEG can be applied to measure the level of physical and mental fatigue among construction workers and assess the safety hazards, such as trips, falls, and impacts, caused by workers' mental and emotional state including depression, and stress, thereby improving health and productivity (Hasanzadeh et al., 2018; Tehrani et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: visual search and attention allocation patterns of workers with different personality traits, knowledge levels, and experience levels
findings.consequent: identification of on-site hazards, analysis of hazard probability due to search defects
findings.quote: Scholars have also employed eye tracking to explore the visual search and attention allocation patterns of workers with different personality traits, knowledge levels, and experience levels (Fu et al., 2022). This approach has enabled effectively identification of on-site hazards, and analysis of the probability of hazards caused by search defects (Hasanzadeh et al., 2017).

findings.antecedent: active safety training for construction workers
findings.consequent: risk alertness, attention levels and risk perception
findings.quote: active safety training for construction workers is imperative to improving their risk alertness, attention levels and risk perception (Choi et al., 2019). Neuroscience tools... are also commonly used to study workers' attitudes and willingness to train safely, assess the degree of improvement in safety hazard recognition ability under different training modes, and establish post-training safety warning as well as job performance assessment systems (Comu et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: architectural elements
findings.consequent: aesthetic effect and observer's gaze pattern
findings.quote: architects usually use eye tracking technology to not only determine the aesthetic effect of architectural elements but also explore the relationship between the observer's gaze pattern with the formal properties of architectural elements under different design parameters (Jam et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: specific design parameters
findings.consequent: key psychological dimensions and neural features evoked
findings.quote: Previous studies have also reported the use of ERP and fMRI in analysis of key psychological dimensions sensitive to specific design parameters and the neural features evoked (Ma et al., 2015; Coburn et al., 2020).

findings.antecedent: proportion of interior functional areas, lighting designs, room color schemes, furniture color and other spatial environment designs
findings.consequent: human emotions, security and comfort
findings.quote: These include the proportion of interior functional areas, lighting designs, room color schemes, furniture color and other spatial environment designs, with respect to human emotions, security and comfort (Tuszynska-Bogucka et al., 2020).

findings.antecedent: different route parameters in a virtual platform
findings.consequent: working memory and cognitive workload during execution of navigation tasks
findings.quote: these data have enabled effective understanding of the working memory and cognitive workload during execution of navigation tasks by designing different route parameters in the virtual platform, and finally propose the optimal route plan for interior design (Vecchiato et al., 2015).

findings.antecedent: demanding physical tasks almost every day (e.g., steelworkers, porters)
findings.consequent: musculoskeletal disorders (low back pain, shoulder pain)
findings.quote: demanding physical tasks almost every day, which take a toll on their health, as evidenced by prevalence of various conditions such as musculoskeletal disorders. For example, Umer et al. (2017) reported that steelworkers suffer from low back pain caused by prolonged static or awkward postures, while Anton et al. (2013) demonstrated that porters suffer from shoulder pain and other bodily pain when carrying various types of loads.

findings.antecedent: construction workers performing repetitive manual tasks
findings.consequent: muscle strength and fatigue
findings.quote: Additionally, EMG can also detect the development of muscle strength and fatigue of construction workers in performing repetitive manual tasks and can predict the degree of muscle fatigue by analyzing the root mean square normalized amplitude of EMG (Li et al., 2017).

findings.antecedent: use of passive exoskeleton systems
findings.consequent: lumbar vertical spine muscle activity
findings.quote: Muscle ergonomics analysis demonstrates that the use of passive exoskeleton systems significantly reduces lumbar vertical spine muscle activity and that the reduction is even greater when weight lifting loads (Antwi-Afari et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: glare
findings.consequent: visual discomfort of indoor personnel
findings.quote: glare is a significant factor affecting the visual comfort of indoor personnel. PUI, BA, FR, and other indicators can indicate visual discomfort caused by glare, but increasing ambient luminance contrast can improve efficiency in a non-glare environment (Liu et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: visual search patterns of workers who correctly identify hazards
findings.consequent: differ from those who do not, with attention deficit and mental fatigue being the primary reasons for workers' decreased ability to detect hazards.
findings.quote: it is discovered that the visual search patterns of workers who correctly identify hazards differ from those who do not, with attention deficit and mental fatigue being the primary reasons for workers' decreased ability to detect hazards.

findings.antecedent: biophilic design elements such as greenery
findings.consequent: occupant's health and performance
findings.quote: biophilic design elements such as greenery are gaining popularity, and the use of eye movement metrics such as total fixation time can help designers better understand how office design can contribute to occupant's health and performance (Guo et al., 2022).

findings.antecedent: thermal perception in the built environment
findings.consequent: arousal and mood
findings.quote: Thermal perception in the built environment is determined by the arousal and mood

findings.antecedent: construction noise, as well as prolonged indoor noise in the building sound environment
findings.consequent: people's minds and bodies
findings.quote: Construction noise, as well as prolonged indoor noise in the building sound environment, can affect people's minds and bodies.

findings.antecedent: varying degrees of illumination and color temperatures in the lighting environment
findings.consequent: people's mental states (reflected by alpha band activity)
findings.quote: The alpha band which is excited by varying degrees of illumination and color temperatures in the lighting environment can reflect people's mental states.

findings.antecedent: poor indoor air quality and high pollution levels
findings.consequent: increased theta and beta powers of the human brain, resulting in bad moods
findings.quote: When indoor air quality is poor and pollution levels are high, theta and beta powers of the human brain increase and can result in bad moods

findings.antecedent: viewing indoor plants
findings.consequent: more active alpha waves of the human brain, significantly relieving personal stress
findings.quote: whereas the alpha waves of the human brain are more active when viewing indoor plants and can significantly relieve personal stress.

findings.antecedent: workers subjected to different stressors during construction
findings.consequent: different brain wave patterns, reflecting emotional state, attention level, mental workload, and other mental activities
findings.quote: When workers are subjected to different stressors during construction, different brain wave patterns are generated, reflecting their emotional state, attention level, mental workload, and other mental activities.

findings.antecedent: monitoring and identification of worker fatigue using EEG
findings.consequent: construction hazards
findings.quote: Monitoring and identification of worker fatigue using EEG can significantly reduce construction hazards

findings.antecedent: specific geometric landscapes
findings.consequent: emotional perception (theta waves in anterior cingulate cortex)
findings.quote: According to research, theta waves in the anterior cingulate cortex are associated with the emotional perception of specific geometric landscapes.

findings.antecedent: prefrontal and hippocampal brain areas
findings.consequent: evaluation of architectural aesthetics
findings.quote: Scholars have discovered that the prefrontal and hippocampal brain areas are involved in the evaluation of architectural aesthetics, with the primary factor affecting the activation of the parahippocampus place area being the openness of the space, which is typically regarded as more beautiful (Chatterjee et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: ceiling height
findings.consequent: aesthetic judgments in architectural design (visuospatial processing activates specific brain regions)
findings.quote: By studying the effect of ceiling height on aesthetic judgments in architectural design, researchers discovered that visuospatial processing activates the left anterior cuneiform and left middle frontal gyrus of the brain (Vartanian et al., 2015).

findings.antecedent: certain contemplative buildings (e.g., museums, churches, libraries, etc.)
findings.consequent: contemplative states (significant activation of specific brain regions)
findings.quote: Specific architectural styles can also induce contemplative states; for example, certain contemplative buildings (e.g., museums, churches, libraries, etc.) cause significant activation of the left posterior central gyrus and left inferior parietal phase, eliciting contemplative experiences (Bermudez et al., 2017).

findings.antecedent: persistent noise exposure
findings.consequent: alter the limbic gyrus (cingulate and parahippocampal gyrus), as well as adhesion locations
findings.quote: Additionally, construction noise has been studied using fMRI, and it was discovered that persistent noise exposure may alter the limbic gyrus (particularly the cingulate and parahippocampal gyrus), as well as adhesion locations, including the anterior cuneus and posterior lobe of the cerebellum (Dai and Lian, 2018).

findings.antecedent: workers' prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity
findings.consequent: hazard recognition ability
findings.quote: fNIRS recordings of workers' prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity reveal a negative association between PFC activity and hazard recognition ability (Zhang et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: different cortical regions of the PFC
findings.consequent: hazard recognition (electrical, shock, stab-related)
findings.quote: During hazard recognition, different cortical regions of the PFC are differentially and continuously activated, with the left PFC being more involved, the dorsolateral PFC is used for electrical and shock-related hazard recognition, and the ventral PFC being used for stab-related hazard recognition (Zhou et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: fall hazards (compared to electrical and fire hazards)
findings.consequent: brain activation and cognitive resources
findings.direction: activate the brain more and use significant
findings.quote: However, when compared to other hazards such as electrical and fire hazards, fall hazards activate the brain more and use significant cognitive resources (Liao et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: real-time cognitive load
findings.consequent: design of adaptive wayfinding systems
findings.quote: Meanwhile, fNIRs are being employed in indoor wayfinding research, where they are used to assist in the design of adaptive wayfinding systems by monitoring and classifying real-time cognitive load (Zhu et al., 2021).
